journeys.label: Anyone buying a report
journeys.sub: No account. Finds a company page, pays, gets a PDF by email.

nodes.label: Company report page
nodes.sees: A page about one company: overview, risks, a free sample if there is one, and the buttons that start every purchase — Download free PDF, Buy ready report, Generate a fresh report. People arrive from Google, from the Reports catalog, or from the site search.
nodes.behind: These pages are built in advance for about 1,200 companies. The catalog at reports.html shows the same choices as cards. The home page and search only lead here; nothing is sold on them.

nodes.label: They choose…
nodes.sees: Three options on the page: open a free PDF, buy a ready report (already written, downloads instantly, €20), or order a fresh report (written on demand, arrives in about 30 minutes, €50). When buying, a small dialog offers to add revision rounds.
nodes.behind: Prices come from Stripe when the page loads, so every page shows the same price.

nodes.label: Reads the free PDF
nodes.sees: The PDF opens straight away. No email, no payment, no account.
nodes.behind: Free reports are ordinary links to the file store. A few reports rotate into the free tier each week to bring in search traffic; the rest cannot be opened without paying, even if someone guesses the address.
dev: api/create-checkout.js:20-22 — a free report cannot be sold

nodes.label: Pays on the Stripe page
nodes.sees: A payment page hosted by Stripe showing the report and the price. They fill in their email and card, or use Google/Apple Pay. The email typed here is where the report will be sent.
nodes.behind: Before this page opens, the site checks the report really is for sale, and — for the revisions option — that this report can be revised at all. Everything the later steps need (which company, ready or fresh, revisions or not) travels with the payment.
dev: the screenshot is an illustration; a real Stripe page needs a live session

nodes.label: Checkout cancelled
nodes.sees: A short 'Checkout cancelled' page with a way back to the catalog. Nothing was charged.
nodes.behind: Nothing was saved — no order, not even the email address.
nodes.gap: There is no reminder email for an abandoned checkout, because there is nothing to send it to.

nodes.label: Payment recorded
nodes.sees: Nothing — this happens in the second after paying, while they are being sent to the thank-you page.
nodes.behind: Stripe tells the site the payment succeeded, and the purchase is saved with the buyer's email. A ready report is emailed at once; a fresh report becomes an order and the writing starts. If saving fails, Stripe keeps retrying until it works, and the same payment is never recorded twice.

nodes.label: Thank-you page
nodes.sees: For a ready report: 'Payment confirmed' and a Download button. For a fresh report: 'Order confirmed', arriving by email in about 30 minutes. If revisions were bought there is also a 'Track order & request a revision' link — that link is the only way into the order page.
nodes.behind: The page asks Stripe whether this payment really went through before showing anything. The download button does not point at the file; it goes through the site, which re-checks the payment on every click.

nodes.label: Email: order confirmed
nodes.sees: 'Order confirmed' — we are writing your report, it will arrive in about 30 minutes. With revisions, this email also carries the 'Track your order' link.
nodes.behind: Only a confirmation. The report itself comes in a second email when it is finished.

nodes.label: Email: your report
nodes.sees: 'Your report is ready' with a Download PDF button — and a 'Request revision' link only if revision rounds were bought.
nodes.behind: The download button uses the same gated link as the thank-you page, so the email keeps working later.
nodes.gap: Someone who bought without revisions gets no revision link at all, so there is no way for them to buy rounds afterwards. Adding that link for every buyer is a small change to the same email.

nodes.label: Report is written · ~30 min
nodes.sees: Nothing, unless they bought revisions and opened the order page — there it says 'Preparing your report…'.
nodes.behind: A background worker imports the company's latest financial data, then asks the report engine to write and lay out the PDF, checking back every few minutes until it is done. If the data import times out it simply tries again next round.
dev: server/lambda/worker.js — runs every 5 minutes and on demand

nodes.label: Downloads the PDF
nodes.sees: The PDF opens or downloads, from the thank-you page or from the email.
nodes.behind: Every download makes a fresh, short-lived link after checking the payment again. There is no permanent file address for a paid ready report.

nodes.label: Email: your report
nodes.sees: 'Your report is ready' with a Download button. This link is permanent and can be used any time later.
nodes.behind: The finished PDF is stored privately and does not appear in the public catalog unless resale is switched on. The email is sent exactly once, even if the worker crashes half-way.

nodes.label: Report could not be written
nodes.sees: Only someone holding the order-page link sees anything: 'Something went wrong — contact support'. Everyone else simply never receives the report email.
nodes.behind: The order is marked failed and an alert email comes to us.
nodes.gap: The customer is never emailed about a failure — somebody has to notice the alert and follow up by hand.

nodes.label: Done — has the report
nodes.sees: Nothing more. Without the revisions option there is no order page and no way to ask for changes.
nodes.behind: The purchase stays recorded and the emailed link keeps working.
nodes.gap: This is the most common ending, and it is a dead end: no upsell, no way to buy revisions later.

nodes.label: Order page
nodes.sees: 'Your report is ready' with the Download button, a box to describe a change in plain language, how many revision rounds are left, and the revision history. While the report is still being written it says 'Preparing your report…' and refreshes itself.
nodes.behind: Reachable only through the link in the thank-you page and the emails — the link carries the payment reference. The page refreshes every 8 seconds. Members reach the same page from the member area with their login instead.

nodes.label: Done — has the report
nodes.sees: Nothing more. Without revisions there is no order page; the emailed link is permanent.
nodes.behind: The PDF stays stored privately. After the resale window (14 days) it is hidden from any resale listing, but the customer's link keeps working.

nodes.label: Done — keeps the link
nodes.sees: Nothing more. The order page and the emailed link keep working, and unused revision rounds stay available.

nodes.label: Asks for a revision
nodes.sees: They type the change in plain language — for example 'assume the gold price doubles in 2027' — and press Request revision. The page switches to 'Revising your report…'.
nodes.behind: The request is checked (not empty, not absurdly long) and one revision round is reserved. If none are left, the page offers to buy more at €5 per round.

nodes.label: No rounds left — offered more
nodes.sees: 'You've used all included revisions', with a Buy more revision rounds button. That opens a small Stripe payment (€5 per round) and returns them to the same page with the rounds added.
nodes.behind: Extra rounds are a separate small purchase attached to the same order.

nodes.label: Report is revised · ~30 min
nodes.sees: 'Revising your report…' on the order page.
nodes.behind: The engine takes the original report plus the customer's comment and produces a new version, with a short memo of what changed — target price, rating, forecasts. The original file is never overwritten.

nodes.label: Revision failed — round given back
nodes.sees: A red notice on the order page: the revision could not be made, the round was not used, please try again. The previous report is still there.
nodes.behind: The order goes back to 'delivered' with the error attached.
nodes.gap: No email is sent when a revision fails, so someone who closed the page never learns about it.

nodes.label: Email: report updated
nodes.sees: 'Your report has been updated', with a Download button for the new version and a link back to the order page.
nodes.behind: Sent once the revised PDF is stored. Every version keeps its own permanent link.

nodes.label: New version on the order page
nodes.sees: The revision history now shows 'Revision 2' at the top: what they asked for, what moved (target price, rating, forecasts) and a download link per version. If rounds remain they can ask again.
nodes.behind: One round is now used. The history stays with the order.

journeys.label: Member on a monthly plan
journeys.sub: Pays every month for picks from the catalog, their own generations, and other analysts' work.

options.label: Take a report from the library

nodes.label: Pricing page
nodes.sees: Four plans side by side: Investor €19/month, Investor Plus €39/month, Company Coverage €59 per company per year, and the free analyst membership. Each lists how many catalog reports, generations, analyst reads and revision rounds it includes.
nodes.behind: The plan limits shown here are the real numbers the system enforces later — reports per month, generations, analyst reads, revision rounds.

nodes.label: Signs in
nodes.sees: Two ways in, side by side: analysts sign in with LinkedIn, subscribers type their email and get a sign-in link. No passwords anywhere.
nodes.behind: The emailed link works for 15 minutes. There is no password to lose or reset.
nodes.gap: Anyone who signs in with LinkedIn currently becomes an analyst — there is no gate on that yet.

nodes.label: Pays for the plan
nodes.sees: A Stripe page for the monthly or yearly subscription. After paying they land back in the member area with the plan active.
nodes.behind: The subscription's state comes from Stripe: a failed card puts the account in a grace period and it still works; a cancellation ends access immediately.
nodes.gap: There is no self-service upgrade, downgrade or cancel — those are emails to support today.

nodes.label: Member area
nodes.sees: One page, not tabs: a strip at the top with their email, plan and how much of each allowance is left, then the report library, other analysts' reports, the monthly generation, buying an extra report, and (for analysts) income.
nodes.behind: Which sections appear depends on the plan and the role. The counters are a per-month record; everything resets on the 1st.

nodes.label: They choose…
nodes.sees: Take one of this month's picks from the catalog, generate a fresh report on a company they choose, buy an extra report beyond the plan, or open another analyst's published analysis.
nodes.behind: Each of these draws on a different allowance, and each is counted separately.

nodes.label: Takes a library pick
nodes.sees: A list of catalog reports they can claim this month. Opening one they have already taken costs nothing.
nodes.behind: Only reports older than 30 days can be picked, so the newest work stays paid-for. Investor gets 3 a month, Investor Plus 10.

nodes.label: Uses the monthly generation
nodes.sees: They pick any listed company and start a report. Investor Plus includes one a month; the plain Investor plan includes none.
nodes.behind: The monthly slot is reserved before the engine starts, so a failure never silently eats it.

nodes.label: Buys an extra report
nodes.sees: 'Another report, on demand' — €40 for members instead of the €50 list price. Paid through Stripe, then it behaves exactly like any fresh report.
nodes.behind: The member price is worked out on the server from their live subscription, not from anything the browser sends.

nodes.label: Opens an analyst's analysis
nodes.sees: Another analyst's published work, included in the plan — 5 reads a month on Investor, 20 on Investor Plus.
nodes.behind: Opening one spends a read and locks the next one until they have rated it and written a couple of sentences about what it adds. That is what produces the analyst ranking.
nodes.gap: These reads earn the analyst who wrote it nothing today — only direct sales do.

nodes.label: Allowance used up — can top up
nodes.sees: The counter that ran out offers a top-up: €5 for an extra report pick, €2 for an extra analyst read, up to 20 at a time. A used-up monthly generation just says so and waits for the 1st.
nodes.behind: Top-ups are added to the same monthly record, so anything bought and not used expires at the end of the month.
nodes.gap: Buying credits late in the month can mean paying for something that expires days later — nothing warns about that.

nodes.label: Report is written · 20–40 min
nodes.sees: The card shows progress and refreshes by itself; they can close the page.
nodes.behind: Member generations go through exactly the same queue and engine as everything a non-member orders.

nodes.label: Reads it
nodes.sees: The report opens. It stays theirs — re-opening later does not spend another pick.
nodes.behind: A claimed report is recorded against the account, so the entitlement outlives the month it was claimed in.

nodes.label: Email: your report
nodes.sees: 'Your report is ready' with a permanent download link, same as any other buyer gets.

nodes.label: Order page
nodes.sees: The same order page a non-member gets, reached from the member area. It shows the download, the revision box and how many rounds the plan includes — 2 on Investor Plus, none on Investor.
nodes.behind: The page uses their login instead of a payment reference. Extra rounds beyond the plan cost €5 each.

nodes.label: Revised report
nodes.sees: The new version appears in the revision history with a note of what changed.
nodes.behind: Same revision machinery as every other order.

nodes.label: Done for this month
nodes.sees: Their allowances tick down; everything resets on the 1st.
nodes.behind: Reports already delivered stay reachable through their links even if the subscription later ends.
nodes.gap: Unused picks, reads and generations do not roll over.

journeys.label: Analyst publishing their own work
journeys.sub: Free membership. Writes with the engine, publishes under their own name, keeps half of what it sells for.

nodes.label: The analyst programme page
nodes.sees: 'Your report. Your name on it. Half of what it earns.' Free membership, a fresh report every month, they set the price, they keep 50% of every sale, and a public dated track record anyone can check.
nodes.behind: The terms page is the binding version: ownership, the 50/50 split, how payment works, takedown, and what happens if they leave.

nodes.label: Signs in with LinkedIn
nodes.sees: One button. Signing in is also how they accept the analyst terms.
nodes.behind: Analyst is a role on the same account as a member subscription — someone can be both, and then keeps the better of each allowance.
nodes.gap: Today any LinkedIn sign-in becomes an analyst. There is no approval step, and that is a known blocker before this goes live.

nodes.label: Analyst workspace
nodes.sees: The member area in analyst mode: this month's generation, other analysts' reports to read and rate, their own published work, and the income panel.
nodes.behind: One open publishing obligation at a time. Until the last generation is published, the next one is locked.

nodes.label: Start from what?
nodes.sees: Either generate a fresh report on a company of their choice, or build on another analyst's published analysis — pay that analyst's price plus a €10 fee and start from their work.
nodes.behind: A fork is copied as its own order with its own revision budget and no inherited file, so revising it can never overwrite the original that everyone else is reading.

nodes.label: Starts this month's report
nodes.sees: They pick a company and start. A banner warns that this commits them to publishing it under their own name.
nodes.behind: The monthly slot is reserved before the engine starts.

nodes.label: Builds on another analysis
nodes.sees: 'Build on this' on a published analysis. One payment covers the other analyst's price plus a €10 derivation fee, and they land in their own copy to reprompt.
nodes.behind: The original analyst gets half of the price part; the €10 is Valuatum's. A fork must be revised at least once before it can be published — an unrevised fork is just the original.
nodes.gap: The buy-or-fork chooser is still a browser prompt box asking you to type 1 or 2.

nodes.label: Engine writes it · 20–40 min
nodes.sees: Progress in the workspace; an email when it is done.
nodes.behind: Same queue and engine as every other report.

nodes.label: Steers it with revisions
nodes.sees: The order page, where they reprompt the report in plain language — up to 5 rounds included, €5 each after that. This is where the analyst's actual judgement goes in.
nodes.behind: The comments they type are, in effect, the published work — the engine writes, the analyst directs.

nodes.label: Publishes it
nodes.sees: They set a price in euros and how many days until it becomes free to read, then publish. It goes out under their own name.
nodes.behind: Company, recommendation and target price are taken from the delivered report, never from the browser, so the listing cannot be gamed. Publishing freezes that PDF — the price can still be changed later, the content cannot.
nodes.gap: Nothing is reviewed before it goes public; moderation happens afterwards.

nodes.label: Steps down instead
nodes.sees: 'Continue without publishing' turns them into an ordinary reader. The report they generated stays private and theirs.
nodes.behind: Refused while a publication is still owed — they cannot walk away from an open obligation.
nodes.gap: If a generation fails outright, the obligation stays open and only an admin can clear it.

nodes.label: Live on the company page
nodes.sees: Their analysis appears in the analyst section of that company's page, with their name on it, and in the member area for other members to read.
nodes.behind: Anyone can buy it — no account needed. Buyers get an email with a permanent link. After the free-after date it opens to everyone.
nodes.gap: Rendering a published analysis onto the company page is the piece still being finished.

nodes.label: Published, no sales yet
nodes.sees: It sits on the company page building their public track record, and members can read it.
nodes.behind: The next monthly generation is unlocked once the obligation is met.
nodes.gap: Member reads earn the analyst nothing today — only direct sales pay. The per-report bounty exists in the code but is switched off.

nodes.label: Someone buys it
nodes.sees: A reader — or another analyst forking it — pays the price the analyst set.
nodes.behind: The buyer gets an emailed permanent link that re-checks the payment.

nodes.label: Taken down by an admin
nodes.sees: The analysis disappears from the public page and the reader is refunded.
nodes.behind: Moderation is after the fact: an admin can take anything down, which voids the sale and claws back the earning.
nodes.gap: There is no admin screen for this yet — it is an API call.

nodes.label: Income panel
nodes.sees: Four figures: paid to you, ready to invoice, held for 14 days, and what your reports sold for.
nodes.behind: Half of every sale is theirs, held 14 days to cover chargebacks and moderation, after which they invoice Valuatum. There is no automatic payout.
nodes.gap: Analysts invoice by hand — no Stripe Connect, no payroll integration.

nodes.label: Paid, and free to write again
nodes.sees: They invoice for what has cleared, and the next monthly generation is open.
nodes.behind: Their public track record grows with every published report, which is the point of the programme.
